gaps.risk: Dedupe decisions made silently by the implementer will each pick differently per surface; this ledger needs Brad or the design lead to sign the seven calls before wave planning.

gaps.title: The formerly-free recipe gate: a warm no instead of a cold wall
gaps.spec: Free recipes rotate every Friday, so links shared in week 30 hit the paywall in week 31; with the share features shipping, this becomes the most common cold-visitor dead end and nobody designed it. On gated recipe pages, the Ghost content CTA slot gets the brand treatment: 'This one went back behind the counter when the free five rotated Friday.' followed by the five currently-free recipes as real cards (build-time from the rotation data, refreshed by the same chain that flips visibility) and the $1 pitch under them. The visitor who came for tonight's dinner leaves with a free dinner either way. Same pass styles the Ghost 404 page (old domain links are dead forever per the no-redirect decision, and typos happen): search box, the free five, links to the board and hub, in the site voice.
gaps.risk: The gated-post CTA renders from the Ghost theme or Portal, not from the post HTML that build-card2 controls; confirm which slot Ghost 6 exposes for paid-gap content before promising per-recipe dynamic cards, else fall back to a static five refreshed weekly by the rotation script.

gaps.title: Handoff arrival moment and unmatched-ingredient honesty
gaps.spec: The Shop This Recipe handoff proposal covers the send side but not the landing. When the board loads with a handoff key, the arrival needs a moment: scroll settles on the trip planner, pre-checked rows pulse once in sequence (the existing cream pulse token), and a dismissible cream banner states the truth: 'Loaded 11 of 13 ingredients from Chicken Bulgogi. We do not track prices for: gochujang, mirin.' Unmatched ingredients are the honest gap in the whole pipeline (recipe items resolve by bid against the feed; some will not match a board commodity) and silently dropping them means someone stands in Aldi missing two ingredients. The unmatched list also links to /suggest-an-item/ prefilled, which is both honest and a request-form growth loop. Persist the banner state so a reload does not re-fire the choreography.
gaps.risk: The bid-to-commodity match rate is unmeasured; if it is low (say under 70%) the banner reads as an apology on every handoff and the feature should not ship until the mapping improves. Measure match rate across all 513 recipes at build time first.

gaps.title: Aisle Mode offline resilience: stores are signal dead zones
gaps.spec: Aisle Mode's spec builds the overlay from in-page data at open, which is right, but nobody stated the constraint: grocery stores have terrible reception, so Aisle Mode must make zero network requests after open and must survive a tab reload. Harden: check-off state persists to localStorage per store per board week on every tap (piggybacks the persistence proposal's storage keys); if the tab reloads inside the store with no signal, the board page is likely bfcache or HTTP-cached, and Aisle Mode re-opens from the persisted state via the resume pill. All assets are inline already (hard constraint), so the only risk is a lazy fetch sneaking in; add a review rule that Aisle Mode's code path contains no fetch(). One line of UI: the overlay footer says 'Works with no signal. Your checkmarks are saved on this phone.' which is both true and a quiet flex no competitor page can make.
gaps.risk: A cold reload without cache on a dead connection still loses the page; that is browser reality, do not promise full offline (no service workers possible under Ghost injection constraints), promise only saved checkmarks.

gaps.title: Keyboard, focus, and screen-reader states for everything the survivors animate
gaps.spec: The motion vocabulary gates on prefers-reduced-motion but no proposal covers focus or announcement states, and the survivors add overlays, bottom sheets, live totals, and custom checkboxes, all of which have accessibility failure modes. One pass in the tokens include: a single :focus-visible style (2px gold outline, 2px offset) on every interactive element; the results line, trip ticker total, and batch-cost total get aria-live=polite so their tweened numbers announce once, not per frame (tween the visual, set the text once at the end); custom checkboxes stay real input[type=checkbox] visually replaced, never divs; row expansion sets aria-expanded; the bottom sheet and Aisle and Cook modes trap focus, close on Escape, and return focus to their trigger (the pushState back-button handling already specced doubles for this). Cheap, invisible when right, and the difference between hand-built and exported when someone tabs through.
gaps.risk: aria-live on a debounced ticker can still chatter if wired per-frame; the announce-once-at-end rule must be in the shared tween helper, not left to each call site.
